written_from: IBM z/OS MVS JCL Reference (SA23-1385) and z/OS DFSMS Using Data Sets, read by section, not page (page numbers are not cited): the DD statement DSNAME parameter (generation data group relative numbers), the DISP parameter (normal / abnormal-termination dispositions, PASS), the EXEC COND parameter, and DFSMS 'Generation data groups' (relative generation resolution at job start, roll-in at job end, LIMIT). The expected answers were written before any evaluator ran on them. Read again 2026-11-19 from the local JCL User's Guide (ieab500_v3r1.txt, Appendix A, 'DSNAME Parameter - GDGBIAS=JOB', p. 236) and the JCL Reference (GDGBIAS parameter, p. 403: GDGBIAS=JOB is the default): the relationship between a relative and an absolute generation is fixed at the first reference in the job, a generation created by (+1) is read in a later step by the same (+1), cannot be read in its own step, and 'at the end of the job' the relative numbers of the group are updated. That answers the old assumption A1 (roll-in at the end of the job); A2 is still assumed.
scenario_input: catalog (or catalog_from: another scenario's catalog_after): per GDG base, limit and the cataloged absolute generations, oldest first. given: per step that starts, {rc: n} or {abend: code}.
scenario_answer: expect: per STEP.DDNAME of each step that runs, the absolute generation number the DD names. catalog_after: per base the cataloged generations, oldest first, after the job ends.
flow_jcl: //* #8413 slice 3: GDG relative generations. Which absolute generation
//* each DD names, and the catalog after the job. The answers are in
//* scenarios.json, written from IBM's z/OS MVS JCL Reference
//* (SA23-1385) and z/OS DFSMS Using Data Sets before any

scenarios.basis: DSNAME, generation data group: (0) is the most recent generation cataloged, (-1) the one before it, (-2) the one before that. With generations 5, 6, 7 cataloged, (0) = 7, (-1) = 6, (-2) = 5. Reading creates nothing, so the catalog is unchanged.

DSNAME: (+1) names the next generation, 8. Every relative number in a job is resolved against the catalog as it stood when the job started, so (+1) in the later step C2 is the same generation C1 created, while (0) is still 7 and (-1) is still 6 (the new generation is not rolled into the catalog until the job ends). At job end 8 is cataloged as the most recent.
A later job sees the catalog the earlier job left: 8 is now (0), 7 is (-1), 6 is (-2).

DSNAME: (+1) is the next generation after the one current at job start (2), so 3; (+2) is the one after that, 4. A later step naming (+1) or (+2) names those same generations; (0) is still 2. Both are cataloged at job end, oldest first.

DISP, abnormal-termination disposition: EOUT is DISP=(NEW,CATLG,DELETE) and E1 abends, so generation 8 is deleted and never cataloged; the PAY.GDG catalog is unchanged. E2 (COND=EVEN) runs after the abend and ends normally, so its (+1) of AUD.GDG, 3, is cataloged.

DISP: when the abnormal-termination disposition is omitted the system applies the normal-termination one. FOUT is DISP=(NEW,CATLG) and E2 abends, so generation 3 is cataloged anyway. E1 ends normally, 8 is cataloged.
EXEC COND: B1 ends RC 8, so (4,LT,B1) is true and B2 is bypassed; a bypassed step allocates none of its DDs, so BOUT creates nothing. B3's (+1) is 8 and is cataloged at job end.
DISP PASS: the generation created by P1 is passed to P2 under the same (+1) name; P2's DISP=(OLD,CATLG) catalogs it, so 8 is cataloged.

Generation data group LIMIT: the group holds at most LIMIT generations (3). Rolling 8 in makes the oldest, 5, drop out of the catalog; whether 5 is also scratched (deleted) depends on the group's SCRATCH / NOSCRATCH attribute and is not answered here. Relative numbers in the job are unchanged by the limit.

DISP, generation data sets (User's Guide, Appendix A, 'DISP parameter'): if you code MOD for a generation data set and the specified relative generation does not exist in the catalog, the system changes the status to NEW. (+1) is not cataloged, so M1's MOUT is a NEW generation, 8, cataloged at job end. M2's MADD names (0), which exists (7), so it stays MOD: it names 7 and creates nothing, and the group's relative numbers are unchanged until job end.
DISP MOD on the absent (+1) is changed to NEW (see mod-plus-one-creates-a-generation), so the DD names generation 8; N1 abends and the abnormal disposition DELETE applies, so 8 is not cataloged.

z/OS DFSMS Using Data Sets, chapter 29 'Processing generation data groups', 'Relative generation number': the absolute number assigned depends on the number last assigned (7) and the relative number (+2), and 'if you have a single step job, and the generation being cataloged is a +2, one generation number is skipped' (8). So S1.SOUT names 9 and 9 is cataloged at job end; 8 is never cataloged.

z/OS DFSMS Using Data Sets, chapter 29 'Processing generation data groups', 'Relative generation number': a relative number 'tells the system the location of an entry representing a previously cataloged generation'. The catalog holds 5, 6, 7, 9, so (0) = 9 and (-1) is the entry before it, 7, not the missing 8; (-2) = 6. ASSUMED (A4): the manual says 'location of an entry' but never works an example across a skipped number.

z/OS DFSMS Using Data Sets, chapter 29 'Processing generation data groups', 'Rolling In a Generation Data Set': 'If a GDG is defined using DEFINE GENERATIONDATAGROUP EMPTY, and is at its limit, then, when a new generation data set is rolled in, all the currently active generation data sets are rolled off.' The group holds 3 of its limit 3, so the roll-in at the end-of-job step leaves only 8. The names in the job are resolved at job start, as in create-then-read-same-job.

z/OS DFSMS Using Data Sets, chapter 29 'Processing generation data groups', 'Rolling In a Generation Data Set': EMPTY empties the group only when it 'is at its limit'. It holds 2 of 3, so 8 is rolled in and nothing rolls off.

z/OS DFSMS Using Data Sets, chapter 29 'Processing generation data groups', 'Rolling In a Generation Data Set': 'Generation data sets can be in a deferred roll-in state if ... they are allocated with a DISP=(NEW,KEEP)', and 'Refer to generation data sets that are in a deferred roll-in state by their relative number, such as (+1), within the job that allocates it.' So K2 reads (+1) = 8, the generation K1 kept; 8 is not rolled into the active group at job end (the active generations stay 5, 6, 7) and waits, to be named by its absolute number in a later job. ASSUMED (A5): the group is system-managed, which is the case the manual's deferred roll-in text describes.

assumed.text: A generation whose creating step abends under (NEW,CATLG,DELETE) is not cataloged, and under (NEW,CATLG) is, per the DISP text; the absolute number is still consumed by that job only (the next job reuses it).

After the system changes MOD to NEW on a (+n) generation, the step-end disposition is read from the coded DISP as it is for a DISP=NEW dataset; the manual states the status change but not that the abnormal-termination subparameter then applies as for NEW.
A negative relative number counts entries of the generation index, so a number skipped by a (+2) is not counted: with 5, 6, 7, 9 cataloged, (-1) is 7.
The GDG is system-managed; the manual states the deferred roll-in of NEW,KEEP only for that case.

refused.construct: two steps of one job creating the same (+n) with DISP=NEW
refused.why: the second allocation names a dataset that already exists; IBM's text for the failure is not answered here

refused.construct: a (+n) read before any step creates it, or (0) / (-n) with no such cataloged generation
refused.why: a JCL or catalog error, not a step-flow answer

refused.construct: a PASSed generation never received by a later step
refused.why: the manual's disposition of an unreceived passed dataset is not answered here

refused.construct: UNCATLG generations, absolute names (G0007V00), the SCRATCH / NOSCRATCH fate of a rolled-off generation
DISP=MOD of (0) / (-n) with that generation not cataloged, or MOD (+n) after the same (+n) was passed
refused.why: the manual says the status becomes NEW but gives no absolute number for (0) / (-n), and a MOD of a generation created earlier in the job is not stated

refused.construct: the (+1) number of a job that follows one that left a generation in deferred roll-in (NEW,KEEP)
refused.why: the manual says the number depends on 'the number last assigned' but not whether a deferred generation counts

refused.construct: a job that never reaches the end-of-job step (a CATLG generation left in deferred roll-in)
refused.why: the manual lists it as a deferred-roll-in cause; the step-flow model only ends jobs normally
